items.detail: Wall Street shrugged off the overnight futures slide: the **Dow** jumped 1,569 points, or 3.03%, to 53,356.12 Wednesday, its best day since April 2025.
items.why: A clear-cut Democratic win removed election uncertainty, and a sharp fall in oil eased inflation worries.

items.detail: The **S&P 500** rose 1.58% to **7,688.62** and the Nasdaq gained 1.44% to 25,736.51, with tech trailing the Dow's broad rally.
items.why: Cheaper oil and lower Treasury yields helped most stocks, while fears of tighter AI rules held back tech.

items.detail: After hours, **AppLovin** rose and **Expedia** fell on their results, and Friday's payrolls report is the next big test for the rally.
items.why: Both companies reported quarterly results after the close.

items.detail: Wall Street's rally did not reach Seoul: South Korea's **Kospi** plunged as much as **8.8%** Thursday, setting off a 20-minute trading halt as SK Hynix and Samsung sank.
items.why: Investors fear a Democratic Congress will tighten rules on AI data centers, which would hurt demand for Korean memory chips.

items.detail: The **Nifty** rose 0.63% to **23,960.60** Wednesday, a fifth straight gain, though trading stayed range-bound and IT was the only sector to fall.
items.why: Softer crude helped metal, FMCG and realty stocks, while IT dropped over 1% as the US election weighed on tech.

items.detail: US small caps caught up: the **Russell 2000** gained 1.58% to **2,856.96** Wednesday, and India's Nifty Smallcap 100 also jumped about 2%.
items.why: Lower yields and cheaper oil favor domestic small companies that borrow more and spend more of their income on fuel.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** recovered from its election-night low and held near **$80,250** Thursday morning, back above $80,000.
items.why: US spot bitcoin ETFs took in $74.6 million Wednesday, ending a three-day outflow streak as stocks rallied.

items.detail: **Ether** climbed back to about **$2,400**, well above Tuesday's $2,234, as election-night selling reversed.
items.why: US spot ether ETFs drew $53 million Wednesday, their first inflow after seven days of outflows.

items.detail: **Solana** bounced to about **$96**, recovering from Tuesday's $90 but still below the $100 level it lost last week.
items.why: Wider risk appetite returned after the election result, though worries about the Binance hack still cap gains.

items.detail: **Gold** surged about 3% to **$4,053.68** Wednesday, back above $4,000, and silver jumped 4.6%.
items.why: The dollar and Treasury yields fell after the Democratic sweep, and gold ETF holdings hit a record.

crossCuttingTheme: Markets read the Democratic sweep as a clear result: falling oil, a weaker dollar and lower yields lifted the Dow, small caps, gold and bitcoin, while fears of tighter AI rules sent Korean chipmakers sharply lower.
